title: Why Your Wi-Fi Password Can Be Cracked in Minutes 📶 #shorts
description:
On most home Wi-Fi (WPA2), when a device connects it exchanges a short handshake with the router. Someone nearby can capture it, take it away and guess passwords offline at huge speed with a graphics card. Short or common passwords fall fast. Protect yourself with a long random passphrase, WPA3 if your router supports it, and WPS turned off. Only ever test networks you own.

📘 More to learn + my projects: https://github.com/HemashreeVI

#CyberSecurity #WiFi #WiFiSecurity #InfoSec #OnlineSafety #TechExplained #shorts

lines: Your Wi-Fi password might take minutes to crack. Without anyone ever logging in.
Here's how, and how to stop it.
Every time a device joins your Wi-Fi, it swaps a short handshake with the router.
Anyone nearby can record that handshake out of the air, and take it home.
Then they guess passwords offline, billions of tries with a graphics card. No router to slow them down.
A short or common password falls in minutes. A long random passphrase could take centuries. Use one, switch to WPA3 if you can, and turn off WPS.
